complete_source_instructions.intro_text:
SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION V, LEVEL 40
F# MINOR PENTATONIC HARMONY AND FIVE-POSITION PHRASING
FIXED NOTES: F# A B C# E | HARMONY: F#m A E D

PURPOSE
Keep the exact five-position map from Levels 34-39, but stop treating the five pitches as equally stable. Hear the active chord,
land on its strongest available tone, preserve F# as the governing tonic, and use the remaining notes as motion.

F# MINOR PENTATONIC
Notes: F# A B C# E
Degrees: 1 b3 4 5 b7

HARMONY
F# minor = F# A C#; all three chord tones are inside the pentatonic pool.
A major = A C# E; all three chord tones are inside the pentatonic pool.
E major = E G# B; E and B are inside, while G# is a marked completion tone.
D major = D F# A; F# and A are inside, while D is a marked completion tone.

CHORD-ROLE MATRIX
Pitch | Over F#m | Over A | Over E | Over D
F#    | R        | 13     | 9      | 3
A     | b3       | R      | 11     | 5
B     | 4        | 9      | 5      | 13
C#    | 5        | 3      | 13     | M7
E     | b7       | 5      | R      | 9

COUNTS
Module A chord-target cells: 240 notes.
Module B nearest-target voice leading: 60 held tones.
Module C five-position phrase studies: 80 notes.
Module D relative-major/minor response pairs: 60 notes.
Module E chord-completion cadences: 60 notes.
Module F eight-bar relative-center study: 32 notes.
Module G controlled improvisation models: 48 notes.
Complete written workout: 580 sounding tones.

========================================================================================================================
complete_source_instructions.module_b_task_text:
MODULE B - NEAREST-TARGET VOICE LEADING THROUGH | F#m | A | E | F#m |
========================================================================================================================
Hold one whole note per bar. Then add two eighth-note pickups before each landing while preserving the printed beat-1 target.
complete_source_instructions.module_b_transfer_text:
TRANSFER ROUTES
| F#m | E | D | E | : F#-E-F#-E; A-B-A-B; C#-B-A-B.
| F#m | A | E | D | : F#-A-E-F#; A-A-B-A; C#-C#-B-F#.
complete_source_instructions.module_c_text:
MODULE C - FIVE-POSITION FOUR-BAR PHRASES
========================================================================================================================
Progression: | F#m | A | E | F#m |. Four quarter notes per bar. Beat 1 is a strong target; the last note is F#.
complete_source_instructions.module_d_text:
MODULE D - RELATIVE-MAJOR / MINOR CALL AND RESPONSE
========================================================================================================================
The first six notes are an A-major call. The next six preserve the opening but redirect the ending to F# minor.
complete_source_instructions.module_e_text:
MODULE E - CHORD-COMPLETION TONES AND CADENCES
========================================================================================================================
D completes D major. G# completes E major. Both are marked * because they are not F#-minor-pentatonic degrees.
P1: D root at A5 finger 2; G# third at D6 finger 3.
P2: D root at G7 finger 2; G# third at B9 finger 3.
P3: D root at e10 finger 2; G# third at B9 finger 1.
P4: D root at D12 finger 2; G# third at G13 finger 3.
P5: D root at B15 finger 2; G# third at e16 finger 3.
complete_source_instructions.module_f_text:
MODULE F - EIGHT-BAR RELATIVE-CENTER STUDY
========================================================================================================================
| A | E | D | A | F#m | A | E | F#m |
Bars 1-4 establish A major. Bars 5-8 re-center the same pitch pool around F# minor.
complete_source_instructions.module_g_text:
MODULE G - CONTROLLED IMPROVISATION MODELS
========================================================================================================================
Every two-bar phrase ends on F#, A, or C#. Replace inner notes only after the beat-1 target schedule is secure.
complete_source_instructions.practice_mastery_text:
PRACTICE PROGRESSION
========================================================================================================================
1. Say the four chord spellings and the five-note role matrix.
2. Play one Module A position with both pick starts.
3. Sustain the three Module B routes, then add pickups.
4. Learn one Module C phrase per session.
5. Pair its A-major call with its F#-minor answer.
6. Add the D and G# completion tones only after the core targets are clean.
7. Perform the eight-bar relative-center shift with and without drones.
8. Improvise through all three progression cards.
9. Record and evaluate whether F# remains the governing tonic.

ERROR DIAGNOSIS
WRONG TARGET: stop on beat 1 and name the chord role.
A SOUNDS LIKE HOME: reduce density and end three phrases on F#.
E OR D IS UNCLEAR: isolate root/fifth or third/fifth target cells.
COMPLETION TONE BLURS: fret D or G# directly before adding a slide or bend.
FRET FISHING: look at the destination before leaving the prior note.
RHYTHM COLLAPSE: return to one quarter note per click.

MASTERY GATE BEFORE LEVEL 41
Name the role of all five pitches over F#m, A, E, and D; play all twenty Module A target cells with both pick starts;
perform three voice-leading routes in every position; complete all five four-bar phrases without losing F# as tonic;
make the A call and F#m answer sound related but differently centered; use D and G# only as intentional completion tones;
perform the eight-bar center shift without a drone; and record one controlled pass through each progression card on two separate days.

pdf_guidance.module_b_transfer_text:
1. Hold one note per bar. 2. Add two eighth-note pickups before each landing. 3. Replace the
pickups while keeping the same destination and rhythmic placement.
Why these routes work
Root route names the harmony directly. Common-tone route minimizes motion. Fifth route keeps
C# stable from F#m to A, moves to B over E, and returns to C# over F#m.
Progression
Route 1
Route 2
Route 3
| F#m | E | D | E |
F# - E - F# - E
A - B - A - B
C# - B - A - B
| F#m | A | E | D |
F# - A - E - F#
A - A - B - A
C# - C# - B - F#
Transfer rule
Use the nearest printed instance of each named pitch in the current position. The destination is fixed; the route and pickup notes are the variable. Do not jump to a favorite root when a closer third or
fifth gives smoother voice leading.
Hear the new chord before moving. A smaller fretboard motion is useful only when the harmonic landing is correct.
pdf_guidance.module_f_center_text:
The final F# must sound more final than the A at bar 4 even though the pitch collection never changed.
 Drone pass
Bars 1-4 over A drone; bars 5-8 over F# drone.
No-drone pass
Remove both drones and preserve the center shift through targets and phrase endings.
A relative-key modulation can occur without changing the pitch pool; the listener follows the harmony, accents, and cadences.

error_diagnosis: SCALE-RUN AUTOPILOT: remove the fill; sustain one target per bar.

source_guidance.overview_text:
SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION V, LEVEL 47
A MAJOR AND A MINOR PENTATONIC MIXING - CHORD-AWARE COLOR CONTROL - FIXED KEY A

PURPOSE
Combine A major pentatonic and A minor pentatonic intentionally without treating their union as a default
eight-note scale. Use A and E as common anchors, control the three color pairs, target the active dominant
chord, preserve the twelve-bar form, and explain every color change after playing it.

PITCH POOLS
A major pentatonic: A B C# E F#    degrees 1 2 3 5 6
A minor pentatonic: A C D E G      degrees 1 b3 4 5 b7
Common tones: A E
Color pairs: C#/C, F#/G, B/D
E7 completion tone: G#* - not a pentatonic member.

COLOR KEY
C = common to both sets; M = major-only; m = minor-only; * = chord-completion tone.

CORE MIXING GRAMMAR
ANCHOR -> COLOR -> CHORD TARGET -> SPACE
Do not run A-B-C-C#-D-E-F#-G as the default exercise. Keep one motif or anchor stable and change one
color decision at a time.

MODULE COUNTS
Module A: 80 sounding tones
Module B: 72 sounding tones
Module C: 80 sounding tones
Module D: 80 sounding tones
Module E: 96 sounding tones
Module F: 48 sounding tones
Module G: 120 sounding tones
Module H: 80 sounding tones
Module I: 144 sounding tones
Module J: 72 sounding tones
Total written workload: 872 sounding tones

========================================================================================================================
source_guidance.practice_mastery_text:
PRACTICE PROGRESSION
1. Name both pitch pools and all three color pairs.
2. Play one position foundation page against an A drone.
3. Complete all C/C# third-control sites.
4. Play the six two-bar switch studies.
5. Complete the four overlap seams.
6. Play all A7, D7, and E7 hybrid target cells.
7. Complete major-question/minor-answer and minor-question/major-answer in all five positions.
8. Play the minor-only and major-only choruses on separate days.
9. Play the mixed chorus and model chorus with beat-one targets intact.
10. Improvise three choruses: minor only, major only, then controlled mixture.

ERROR DIAGNOSIS
CHROMATIC SOUP: return to A or E and select one color pair only.
WEAK BARLINE: hold the next chord tone for a whole note.
C/C# BLUR: play both fretted targets before bending or sliding.
G# OVERUSE: restrict G# to E7 or a direct E7 approach.
MOTIF LOST: keep the rhythm and change only the final two notes.
FORM LOST: play one root-only chorus and count every bar aloud.

MASTERY GATE
- Name every color note and its set membership.
- Match C# at all six third-control sites.
- Complete all switch studies and overlap seams.
- Make A7, D7, and E7 audible through hybrid target cells.
- Perform minor-only, major-only, and mixed twelve-bar choruses without losing form.
- Record one mixed chorus and explain every major/minor color decision afterward.

NEXT LEVEL
Level 48 combines form, chord targeting, major/minor color, blues vocabulary, motif development, space,
and call-and-response into a three-chorus improvisation synthesis.
